answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded): In the Barcelona province, the gardening introduction pathway shows two distinct prevalence styles conditioned by a single underlying habitat-context gradient — lowland human footprint versus upland naturalness — but expressed on different axes.

(1) FREQUENCY STYLE — pervasive but concentrated in lowland, warm, human-modified habitats: gardening-introduced species occur in the largest fraction of plots in Urban (48%), Wetlands (50%), Coastal (45%), Riparian (36%) and Croplands (21%), and rarely/never in high-elevation natural habitats (Meadows 8%, Coniferous 6.5%, Broad-leaved 4.4%, Scrublands 1.9%, Rock outcrops 0%). Occurrence is conditioned by lowland climate and road/urban proximity: 38% of plots <200 m hold gardening species vs 0% above 900 m; a joint logistic (n=632) leaves only elevation (OR 0.29 per 1 SD, p<0.001) and distance-to-road (OR 0.72 per SD) significant, while raw urbanization is a strong single predictor (OR 1.85 per SD) that is absorbed by elevation because urban plots sit on low ground. Fisher exact: gardening-occurrence odds are ~20x higher in lowland-humanized than upland-natural habitats (p<1e-30).

(2) DOMINANCE STYLE — a minority where invasion is intense, but exclusive where it is rare: conditional on a plot being invaded, gardening is a demographic minority of the local introduced flora in the most humanized/intensively used contexts (mean share: Croplands 0.17, Urban 0.29) where unintentional introductions dominate, yet it becomes the majority or sole introduced flora in less-humanized natural contexts (Wetlands 0.65, Coastal 0.53, Riparian 0.44, Coniferous 0.90, Broad-leaved 1.00). A weighted binomial GLM over 191 invaded plots shows gardening share decreases with surrounding urban cover (OR 0.73 per SD, p<0.001) and cropland cover (OR 0.67, p<0.001) and increases with distance from roads (OR 1.22, p<0.001); tercile contrasts corroborate the agricultural effect (share 0.23 in the high-cropland tercile vs 0.37 baseline, p=0.024).

(3) COMPOSITION + TEMPORAL BACKING: gardening-imported species are predominantly woody/perennial horticultural taxa (20 shrubs/trees + 18 perennial forbs of 42 species), tall (mean 6.5 m), with narrow invaded-niche breadth (0.45) and short mean residence time (86 y), consistent with ornamental escapes; and gardening is the dominant introduction route only in the most recent period (75% of 1985–2019 introductions; 65% of all gardening records), i.e., the "frequent-but-minority" lowland style is recent and tied to ornamental planting, while its rare-but-exclusive upland-forest presence reflects isolated horticultural escapes at the edges of humanized lowlands.

SYNTHESIS: the gardening pathway's prevalence styles shift from "pervasive but outnumbered by unintentional introductions" in lowland, warm, urbanized, road-proximal habitat types to "sparse but dominant/exclusive" in high-elevation, cool, natural, isolated habitat types.

payload.hypothesis: The gardening pathway is frequent, recent and numerically secondary in lowland, warm, urbanized, road-proximal habitats (Urban, Wetlands, Coastal, Riparian, Croplands) but rare and demographically dominant/exclusive (often the only introduced species) in high-elevation, cool, natural, isolated habitat types (forests, scrublands, meadows, rock outcrops) — i.e., its prevalence styles shift from 'pervasive but outnumbered by unintentional introductions' in lowland human-impacted contexts to 'sparse but exclusive' in upland natural contexts, driven respectively by elevation/road-proximity (occurrence) and by land-use intensity — urban and cropland cover — (dominance).
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded/validated 4 assets (632 plot-level records sum exactly to n.total; 81 species; 12-row temporal table). 2) Per-habitat prevalence: occurrence % (frequency) and n.gard/n.total among invaded plots (dominance). 3) VIF/collinearity; retained elevation as climatic-xeric proxy (dropped temp/rainfall, r~0.9-0.96). 4) Logistic regression of gardening occurrence on environmental context across 632 plots. 5) Weighted binomial GLM (quasibinomial-corrected SE) of per-plot gardening share among 191 invaded plots. 6) Supporting: species trait profiles per pathway, temporal backdrop (post-1985 surge), habitat context profiles. 7) Figures (6 SVG) and result tables. All code executed in-workspace; artifacts under analysis/ and outputs/.
